title: Synergistic Inhibition of DNMT and HDAC to Elicit Immunogenic Neoantigens in AML
hypothesis: Combinatorial inhibition of DNA methyltransferases (DNMTs) and histone deacetylases (HDACs) will synergistically reactivate endogenous retroviral elements in AML cells, leading to the expression of immunogenic neoantigens and subsequent immune-mediated tumor lysis.
candidate_intervention_or_focus: Combination therapy with DNMT inhibitors (e.g., Decitabine) and HDAC inhibitors.
mechanistic_rationale: Evidence suggests that simultaneous DNMT and HDAC inhibition can induce immunogenic neoantigens from endogenous retroviral elements, potentially eliciting a T-cell response against AML cells. This approach targets epigenetic dysregulation to enhance anti-tumor immunity. (ER01, ER09 in A01)
falsifiable_predictions: AML cells treated with combined DNMT and HDAC inhibitors will show increased expression of retroviral elements and neoantigens compared to single-agent treatment.
Immunohistochemical analysis will reveal increased T-cell infiltration in tumors treated with the combination therapy.
In vitro co-culture assays will demonstrate enhanced killing of AML cells by T-cells when the AML cells have been pre-treated with combined DNMT and HDAC inhibitors.
key_assumptions: AML cells express relevant endogenous retroviral elements that can be epigenetically silenced.
The re-expressed elements will be processed and presented as neoantigens by AML cells.
The AML patient immune system is capable of recognizing and responding to these neoantigens.
first_validation_step: In vitro testing of combined DNMT and HDAC inhibitors on AML cell lines for neoantigen expression and T-cell recognition.
must_verify_later: Clinical efficacy in AML patient cohorts.
Optimal dosing and scheduling of combination therapy.
